issues.description: Filter '*.exe' on browsefile excludes valid conda executables on macOS/Linux
issues.detail: The create_browsefile call uses filters='*.exe', which is a Windows-only extension. On macOS and Linux, conda/mamba/micromamba binaries have no extension, so users will be unable to select them through the file dialog without manually typing the path. The filter should be platform-aware or default to all files.

issues.description: validate_conda substring match wrongly accepts any path containing 'conda'/'mamba'
issues.detail: The check `tool in out.decode().lower()` runs against --version output but 'conda' and 'mamba' are common substrings. More importantly, a non-conda executable whose --version output happens to include these words (e.g. tools mentioning them) would validate. Consider a stricter prefix or regex match on the version output's first token.

On Windows, os.access(path, os.X_OK) reliably returns True only for files with executable extensions and is generally unreliable. Combined with the '*.exe' filter, this may still reject legitimate conda.bat/conda.exe paths in some configurations. The X_OK check is unnecessary since run_program will fail anyway if it isn't executable.

issues.description: conda_path written to disk even when custom_conda is unchecked
issues.detail: The browsefile is disabled but its config value persists. If a user types a path, unchecks the box, then re-checks it later, the old path silently reactivates. More importantly the empty-string special case in validate_conda returning True means an empty path passes validation even when custom_conda is True, leading to the same 'not found' error users were already trying to fix.

Paths with ~ or environment variables (e.g. ~/miniconda3/bin/conda) will not be expanded before os.path.isfile and run_program calls. Users frequently paste such paths. Apply os.path.expanduser/expandvars in validate_conda and where conda_path is consumed in kernelspec.py.

issues.description: Unconditional setFocus after file selection may affect unrelated dialogs
issues.detail: The change in widgets/config.py adds edit.setFocus() after every file selection in create_browsefile-derived dialogs, not just the new conda field. This subtly changes focus behavior in every existing preferences page that uses select_file and could disrupt keyboard navigation flows elsewhere.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful custom Conda executable option, but several issues should be addressed before merge. The file dialog filter is Windows-only, blocking macOS/Linux users from browsing. The validation logic is loose (substring matching on --version output) and the empty-path early-return undermines the feature when custom_conda is enabled with no path set. The unconditional setFocus change in widgets/config.py affects every existing browsefile usage, which is a wider blast radius than the PR scope.
